findings.title: Router duty packed into one run-on sentence
findings.problem: The Router's duties (intent, constraints, safety level, fixed-sentence ids, a second read for buried requests, and follow-up lookup) are compressed into one dense pipeline bullet, which makes its role harder to parse than the rest of the prompt.
findings.proof: It writes no reply. A message it would answer with fixed sentences alone is read once more by a model for a buried product request;
findings.fix: Split the Router stage into separate sub-bullets: outputs, the no-reply rule, the buried-request re-read, and the follow-up lookup rule.

findings.title: No input-side control for names and street addresses
findings.problem: The input screen redacts e-mail, phone, card and ID numbers but has no step for names or street addresses, which the prompt leaves to the model under the safety policy; no redaction rule or pattern exists for them in the system prompt.
findings.fix: Add a named-entity or address detection step to the input screen in the system prompt, with a placeholder and a pii_note trigger, so names and addresses do not depend on model compliance.

findings.title: Budget limit contradicts automatic 25% and full budget removal in catalog tool
findings.problem: The system prompt says the budget stays the limit, but the catalog tool schema loosens the budget by 25% and then removes it entirely, so the two rules conflict unless the reply always flags it.
findings.proof: the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: State in the system prompt's Search rule that loosened budgets are flagged in constraint_notes and must be said in the reply, and that removal is only allowed when the shopper has not stated a budget.

findings.title: Tool loosening rules restated in full inside rag.search description
findings.problem: The rag.search description contains a long multi-clause loosening block that repeats behaviour the system prompt already describes, and the description is longer than the parameter guidance needs.
findings.proof: Loosening: when fewer products than `top_k` meet every filter, filters are loosened in this order until enough are found
findings.fix: Shorten the description to the call-time guidance (when to call, how to set filters, what is never loosened) and keep the full loosening order in one place.

findings.title: No grounding rule for live results missing price or stock
findings.problem: The context does not say what the Answerer should write when a web result carries no price, stock status or rating, so the model may fill the gap from memory.
findings.fix: Add a rule that any missing price, stock status or rating is written as 'not stated' in the cell, with a fixed sentence for the case.

findings.title: Instruction-stripping depends solely on the MCP server
findings.problem: Removal of instruction-like text from tool results is delegated entirely to the MCP server, with no in-prompt check on catalog listings if that server fails to strip text.
findings.proof: The MCP server removes instruction-like text from tool results (catalog listings and web results) before any model sees it
findings.fix: Add a fallback in the Retriever's code path that rejects or flags any listing containing instruction-like patterns before it reaches a model.

findings.title: Spoken short-form fixed replies duplicate the full list
findings.problem: The short-form spoken versions repeat each fixed reply in near-identical wording, doubling about eleven entries in the knowledge file.
findings.proof: Spoken before a product answer, these are shortened so that the reply still fits 15 seconds:
findings.fix: Store one entry per id with an optional short form field, instead of a second parallel list.

findings.title: System prompt restates catalog loosening already in tool schema
findings.problem: The Search bullet in the system prompt repeats the catalog tool's loosening behaviour, which the tool schema already defines.
findings.proof: the catalog tool loosens some (never a stated age range or a safety exclusion)
findings.fix: Replace the restatement with a pointer to the tool schema and keep only the reply-side obligation to say what each product misses.

findings.title: Catalog size repeated between knowledge file and tool description
findings.problem: The catalog's size, brand count and snapshot date are stated in the knowledge file and again in the rag.search description.
findings.proof: Amazon Product Dataset 2020, cleaned: 9,740 products from 2,204 brands, one snapshot from January 2020.
findings.fix: Keep the catalog size in one file only and reference it from the other.

metadata.business_case: A shopper speaks or types a request. It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
